To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the myocardial infraction following coronary artery occlusions is significantly reduced in rats that are subjected to physical exercise and that the myocardial damage is more severe in rats with aortic banding than in rats that are not subjected to any intervention.

the infarction after standardized coronary occlusion was significantly smaller in rats with myocardium hypertrophy due to swimming exercise than in rats with myocarditis induced by aortic stenosi, that the infarctions in normal control rats were of intermediate size and that the infarct size was highly variable in the individual heart.
the myocardial infraction size following standardized coronary artery ligation is significantly smaller in swimming-exercised than in pressure-loaded rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of physical exercise, and in particular swimming exercise, on the myocardial blood vessels.
the effects of exercise training on myocardial infarct size in rats with aortic banding.
the effect of increased cardiac work on the size of the myocardium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size of the myocardium infarction following a standardized coronary occlusion is smaller in swimming-exercised than in aortic-stenosed rats, and in normal rats than in aortic stenosed rats.
the size of the myocardium infarction is smaller in the exercised animals than in the nonexercised animals and that this difference is probably due to the capillary neoformation.

swimming exercise, by inducing capillary growth in the myocardium, may limit the damage to the myocardium following coronary artery occlusions, whereas the lack of such a reaction in pressure-induced myocardial hypertrophy may make it more vulnerable to the effects of a coronary occlusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the size of myocardium infarction following a coronary artery occlusion is dependent on the size of the myocardium, and the size of the heart, and the size and the size and distribution of myocardial infartion.
physical exercise may be of benefit in the treatment of coronary artery disease.
the myocardial infraction is significantly reduced in rats with myocardium hypertrophy induced by swimming exercise, but not by pressure load, compared with normal rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the size of the myocardium and the size of the heart can be measured by using a 3D ultrasound.
exercise can help prevent heart attacks.
exercise is good for the heart, and that exercise-induced changes in the heart may be beneficial in the event of a myocardial infarct.
